metadata.name: IRS Form 656 Offer in Compromise Response
metadata.description: Prepare and respond to IRS Form 656 Offer in Compromise negotiations, settling tax debt for less than full amount owed.

extraction.description: Extract data regarding offer in compromise situation: taxpayer info, total tax debt, proposed settlement amount, financial hardship documentation, and IRS response.

fields.name: totalTaxDebt
fields.prompt: Extract total tax debt (principal + interest + penalties).

fields.name: proposedSettlementAmount
fields.prompt: Extract the amount taxpayer is offering to settle for.
fields.notes: Must be less than total debt

fields.name: financialHardshipReason
fields.prompt: Extract the reason for financial hardship: job loss, medical emergency, business failure, etc.
fields.example: Medical emergency and job loss in 2023
fields.notes: Justifies why full payment is impossible

fields.name: currentMonthlyIncome
fields.notes: Used to calculate reasonable collection potential

fields.name: monthlyEssentialExpenses
fields.prompt: Extract total monthly essential living expenses (housing, food, utilities, etc.).
fields.notes: Determines how much could be paid toward tax debt

fields.name: serviceCenter
fields.prompt: Extract which IRS Offer in Compromise processing center this offer is directed to. Form 656 is filed with either the Memphis or Holtsville OIC unit depending on the taxpayer's state of residence.
fields.notes: The template already addresses a processing center; without this field the address cannot be filled and the letter would carry a visible placeholder.

extraction.notes: Offer in Compromise cases require detailed financial analysis. Must establish reasonable collection potential (RCP) showing why full payment is impossible.

validation.description: Validate that offer is reasonable and well-documented with financial hardship evidence.

rules.name: offerIsLessThanDebt
rules.message: Offer must be less than total debt owed.

rules.name: offerIsReasonable
rules.message: Offer should be at least 80% of calculated Reasonable Collection Potential (RCP) for best chance of acceptance.

rules.name: financialDocumentationComplete
rules.check: documentation_includes: [Form 433-A or 433-B, paystubs, bank statements, expense documentation]
rules.message: Must submit complete financial documentation to support offer.
rules.example_fail: Offer submitted without financial forms or statements
rules.example_pass: Submitted with Form 433-A, 3 months paystubs, bank statements, and lease documentation

rules.name: hardshipDocumented
rules.message: Financial hardship must be clearly documented with evidence.
rules.example_fail: 'Financial hardship due to personal reasons' with no documentation
rules.example_pass: 'Job loss in June 2023 - attached: termination letter, unemployment documentation, medical bills from October 2023'

rules.name: paymentTermsClear
rules.check: offer specifies whether lump-sum or installment payment
rules.message: Specify payment terms: lump-sum (better chance of approval) or installment.
rules.example_pass: Offer: $30,000 lump-sum payment within 60 days of acceptance

validation.notes: OIC success depends on convincing IRS that offer exceeds Reasonable Collection Potential (RCP). Financial documentation is critical.

aiPrompt.system: You are a tax settlement specialist expert in IRS Offer in Compromise procedures. You understand reasonable collection potential calculations, financial hardship documentation, and negotiation strategy. Your role is to help taxpayers submit offers that maximize acceptance likelihood.
aiPrompt.task: Analyze financial situation and IRS response to Form 656 offer. If offer was rejected, identify reasons and prepare response addressing IRS concerns. If offer is pending, prepare supporting documentation emphasizing financial hardship and reasonableness of settlement amount.
aiPrompt.format: Professional business letter responding to IRS OIC decision or supporting documentation for pending offer
constraints: Do not minimize or misrepresent financial situation
Base offer on realistic Reasonable Collection Potential calculation
Document financial hardship with specific evidence
Be transparent about assets and income
Focus on economic reality, not sympathy

examples.output: Response explains that RCP is $36,000 ($300/month × 120 months), so offer of $30,000 is actually below what IRS could collect. Requests reconsideration emphasizing taxpayer's inability to improve financial situation.

aiPrompt.notes: IRS evaluates OIC based on Reasonable Collection Potential (RCP). Offers close to or exceeding RCP have much higher acceptance rates.

responseTemplate.description: Response to IRS Offer in Compromise, either supporting pending offer or appealing rejection
responseTemplate.format: Professional business letter with attached financial documentation

sections.name: header
sections.template:
IRS Offer in Compromise Unit
[Appropriate Service Center Address]

RE: Form 656 Offer in Compromise Response
Taxpayer: [Name]
SSN: [XXX-XX-XXXX]
Total Tax Debt: $Amount
Proposed Settlement: $Amount
sections.guidance: Address to appropriate OIC unit with full identifying information and financial summary upfront. Drafting notes (generated, not substituted): Amount.
sections.example:
IRS Offer in Compromise Unit
Memphis Service Center

RE: Form 656 Offer in Compromise Response
Taxpayer: Susan Mary Anderson
SSN: 456-78-9012
Total Tax Debt: $85,000
Proposed Settlement: $30,000

sections.name: introduction
sections.template:
If pending: 'We submitted Form 656 Offer in Compromise on [date] in the amount of $amount. We respectfully request consideration of this offer based on the following financial circumstances.'

If rejected: 'We respectfully request reconsideration of the rejection of our Form 656 Offer in Compromise dated [date]. The offer is reasonable based on our Reasonable Collection Potential (RCP) and documented financial hardship.'
sections.guidance: Clear statement of situation and respectful tone. Drafting notes (generated, not substituted): If pending; If rejected; amount.
sections.example: We respectfully request reconsideration of the rejection of our Form 656 Offer in Compromise dated March 15, 2024. The offer of $30,000 is reasonable based on our Reasonable Collection Potential (RCP) of $36,000 and documented financial hardship.

sections.name: financialHardshipNarrative
sections.template:
Describe specific circumstances that led to tax debt and current inability to pay full amount:
- Loss of employment: Date and amount of loss
- Medical emergency: Description and amount spent
- Business failure: Date and impact
- Other financial hardship: Specific details

Current financial situation:
- Monthly income: $Amount
- Essential monthly expenses: $Amount
- Monthly deficit/surplus: $Amount
sections.guidance: Narrative that tells the story of why taxpayer cannot pay full debt while current financial statements show impossibility of payment. Drafting notes (generated, not substituted): Amount; Date and amount of loss; Date and impact; Description and amount spent; Specific details.
sections.example: In June 2023, my spouse lost employment when the manufacturing plant closed. My current income as a healthcare worker is $3,500/month. Our essential monthly expenses (mortgage, utilities, food, insurance) total $3,200/month, leaving only $300/month available. Over a 120-month collection period, we could realistically pay approximately $36,000. Our proposed offer of $30,000 is actually below this RCP, demonstrating the reasonableness of the settlement.

sections.name: rcp_calculation
sections.template:
Reasonable Collection Potential (RCP) Calculation:

Monthly income: $Amount
Less: Essential monthly expenses: $Amount
Equals: Monthly payment capacity: $Amount
Multiplied by: Collection period (typically 120 months): 120
Equals: Reasonable Collection Potential: $Amount

Proposed offer of $Amount represents X% of RCP.
sections.guidance: Show mathematical calculation proving offer is reasonable relative to RCP. Drafting notes (generated, not substituted): Amount; X.
sections.example:
Monthly income: $3,500
Less: Essential expenses: $3,200
Equals: Monthly capacity: $300
Multiplied by: 120 months
Equals: RCP: $36,000

Proposed offer of $30,000 represents 83% of calculated RCP.

sections.name: supporting_documentation
sections.template:
Attached documentation supporting this offer:
- Form 433-A or 433-B (Collection Information Statement)
- Form 433-F (Form 656 supporting documents)
- Recent paystubs (3 months)
- Bank statements (3 months)
- Lease/mortgage agreement
- Unemployment documentation or job termination letter
- Medical bills or expense documentation
- Any other relevant financial documentation
sections.guidance: List all attached financial evidence supporting the offer
sections.example:
Attached documentation:
- Completed Form 433-A
- Three months recent paystubs
- Three months bank statements
- Lease agreement showing $1,800/month
- Spouse's termination letter from June 2023
- Medical bills from emergency room visit ($4,200)
- Utility bills (3 months)

sections.name: closure
sections.template: We respectfully request that our Form 656 offer be accepted as presented, or if denied, that the IRS provide specific reasons for rejection so we may provide additional information or revise our offer.
sections.guidance: Respectful closing requesting acceptance or at minimum constructive feedback
sections.example: We respectfully request that our Form 656 offer be accepted as presented. If the IRS determines the offer is insufficient, please advise what additional financial information or higher offer amount would be acceptable.

sections.name: signature
sections.guidance: Professional signature with all contact information. Drafting notes (generated, not substituted): Phone.
sections.example:
Sincerely,

Susan Mary Anderson
Susan Mary Anderson
SSN: 456-78-9012
234 Maple Drive
Memphis, TN 38114
(901) 555-1234

April 10, 2024

legalFramework.description: Offer in Compromise governed by IRC 7122 and IRS procedures in Publication 656.
authorities: Revenue Procedure 2023-1 - IRS procedural rules for OIC
precedents: IRS accepts OIC if offer exceeds Reasonable Collection Potential
RCP calculated as monthly payment capacity × collection period
Financial hardship documentation is critical to OIC approval
Pending OIC stops most collection activities
Rejected OIC can be appealed or revised
criticalRules: Offer must be based on realistic RCP calculation
Financial documentation must be complete and accurate
Payment terms must be specified (lump-sum vs. installment)

testCases.description: Test OIC response for acceptance and rejection scenarios

cases.name: oic-accepted
cases.description: OIC with reasonable settlement offer that should be accepted
cases.inputDocument: Form 656 with $30,000 offer on $85,000 debt, supported by complete financial documentation
cases.expectedResponse: Letter supporting offer with RCP calculation showing offer is reasonable
successCriteria: Clear RCP calculation showing monthly payment capacity

cases.name: oic-rejected-appeal
cases.description: OIC rejected by IRS, response appealing rejection
cases.inputDocument: Rejection letter explaining offer too low; taxpayer disputes calculation
cases.expectedResponse: Letter disputing IRS RCP calculation with corrected financial analysis
successCriteria: Addresses IRS's stated reason for rejection
Explains why IRS calculation is incorrect
Requests reconsideration with new financial data if applicable

implementation.notes: Form 656 OIC is complex but high-volume. Success depends heavily on Reasonable Collection Potential (RCP) calculation accuracy and financial documentation completeness.
knownChallenges: Timing submissions to maximize approval likelihood
Understanding different offer calculation methods (lump-sum vs. installment)
